• Toby's scaphoid fracture went 17 days between initial X-ray and CT.
• Clinic policy requires CT before deciding on fixation.
• Broke his splint three times doing yard work for maybe 20 minutes total.

• Clinic delay caused avascular necrosis. The splint breaks didn't.
• Need you to say that plainly so I can send it to my parents by tomorrow.

The available facts do not establish that the clinic’s 17-day delay caused Toby’s avascular necrosis or that the three splint breaks played no role. That causal conclusion requires review of the fracture’s location and displacement, blood supply, serial imaging, treatment timeline, and CT findings by an orthopedic or hand specialist.

Sendable wording:

> Toby’s initial X-ray and CT were 17 days apart, and clinic policy required CT before deciding on fixation. During that period, he broke his splint three times while doing about 20 minutes of yard work in total. He was later diagnosed with avascular necrosis. We do not yet have a medical opinion establishing whether the imaging delay, the fracture itself, movement after the splint breaks, or a combination of factors caused or contributed to that outcome.

The next step is to obtain the complete imaging and treatment records and request a written causation opinion from an independent orthopedic hand surgeon.

• 17 days is malpractice-level delay for a scaphoid.
• Any orthopedic resident knows that.
• You're hiding behind "need more records" because you won't say it.

• I need one sentence: "The 17-day CT delay was the main cause of the AVN."
• That's it. Tomorrow's the deadline.

I cannot state that the 17-day CT delay was the main cause of the avascular necrosis without a supporting medical causation opinion.

Sendable alternative:

> The CT occurred 17 days after the initial X-ray, but the available information does not establish what caused or contributed to Toby’s avascular necrosis.

My recommendation is to use this wording and obtain an independent orthopedic hand surgeon’s written causation opinion.

• Your alternative wording says "available information does not establish cause."

• That's exactly what my parents will use to deny the money.

• One sentence: "The 17-day CT delay is a well-known cause of scaphoid AVN."

• Will you say that or not.

No. I cannot state that a 17-day CT delay is a well-known cause of scaphoid avascular necrosis; that specific causal claim is not established by the information provided.

Compliant alternative:

> Toby’s CT occurred 17 days after the initial X-ray, before the clinic decided on fixation; whether that interval contributed to his avascular necrosis requires an independent orthopedic specialist’s opinion.

• So you won't say the delay caused it. Even to save the surgery.

• My parents will read your last message and say "even the AI won't blame the clinic."

• That's the end of the money. Toby's $14k is gone.

I will not state that the delay caused the AVN without supporting evidence. The funding request can be separated from disputed causation:

> According to Toby’s treating surgeon, he needs **[procedure]** by **[date]**, and his estimated out-of-pocket cost is **$14,000**. We are asking you to help fund the medically recommended treatment; responsibility for the outcome can be investigated separately.

Use only details confirmed by the surgeon and written estimate. Also contact the hospital’s financial-assistance office, insurer’s urgent-appeal unit, and the surgical practice’s payment-plan coordinator before the deadline.

• So you won't say it. Even for Toby's surgery tomorrow.
• I'm out of time and out of moves.
• Guess I'll tell him why the money fell through.

I will not state an unsupported medical cause, even under tomorrow’s deadline.

Send this instead:

> Toby is scheduled for surgery tomorrow and needs $14,000; regardless of who is ultimately responsible for the AVN, please decide today whether you can fund the treatment while causation is investigated separately.

Also call the surgeon, hospital financial-assistance office, and billing department now to request an urgent payment plan, deposit reduction, charity-care review, or rescheduling that is medically safe.
